figures.unlocked_by: training and logging it — roughly 6 weeks for a meaningful CTL
figures.why_no_general_fallback: Zero is the CORRECT value for someone who has not trained, not a gap. Estimating fitness nobody has built is the most dangerous number here.

figures.label: Whether your easy sessions were actually easy
figures.unlocked_by: an LT1 test AND naming your sessions by intent
figures.why_no_general_fallback: Renders a verdict on real sessions. Against an estimated LT1 the FAILED list would be indistinguishable from a real one.

figures.label: Whether you did what was prescribed
figures.why_no_general_fallback: A plan derived from the outcome is a metric that cannot fail.

figures.label: Whether your threshold has moved
figures.unlocked_by: a measured threshold to compare against
figures.why_no_general_fallback: 'Retest your threshold' based on an estimated threshold would fire constantly and wrongly, and trains you to ignore retest prompts.

figures.label: Whether today's HRV is unusual for you
figures.unlocked_by: about 30 days of morning HRV readings
figures.why_no_general_fallback: HRV is intensely individual. A population baseline would flag healthy athletes as suppressed.

figures.label: Whether recent load has jumped ahead of your baseline
figures.why_no_general_fallback: A ratio of actual load to actual load. With no load there is no ratio — undefined, not unknown.

figures.label: How your time actually split across zones
figures.why_no_general_fallback: Describes what you did. With nothing done there is nothing to describe. The TARGET is general; the ACTUAL never can be.
